criticalSample.note: Many critics did not provide a numeric score, so the app reports the sample composition rather than inventing a star average.

reception.note: Platform averages describe overall reader approval. They do not reveal what readers thought about a particular collision, and different platforms are shown separately rather than blended.

coverage.saturation: The tenth review reinforced themes already present in the earlier reviews and added no new assessed disagreement. One trade review remains as a holdout check before release.

candidates.question: Is Beth a sympathetically complex heroine or an unlikeable, immature one?
candidates.positionA: Rebecca Munro found Beth so convincingly drawn that even her bad choices retain a sense of tragic beauty.
candidates.positionB: Doreen found Beth selfish, self-absorbed and emotionally immature, and saw no convincing emotional growth over the course of the story.
reasons: Both positions assess the same feature: whether Beth’s flaws deepen her characterization or make her difficult to support.
The surrounding text preserves each reviewer’s qualification rather than reducing either view to a slogan.
Claude assessed attribution, qualifications, disagreement, member wording and source independence as supported.

candidates.question: Do the plot developments feel surprising or predictable?
candidates.positionA: One review found many twists unexpected.
candidates.positionB: Another found much of the story predictable.
reasons: The positive review later says the story depends on a single miscommunication, which weakened its praise of the plotting.
The negative review’s predictability criticism applies mainly to foreshadowed character behaviour, not every twist.
The original collision therefore flattened important qualifications and is blocked.

candidates.question: Is the prose disciplined and restrained, or does it become too explanatory?
candidates.positionA: Seattle Book Mama described the writing as disciplined, restrained and intimate.
candidates.positionB: Bean’s Book Blog found that the writing became overly explanatory in the second half.
reasons: The source passages support a genuine disagreement about the same aspect of prose style.
The corrected wording removes ‘elegant’, which was not present in the cited passage.
Claude’s separate rerun assessed attribution, qualifications, disagreement, member wording and source independence as supported.

excluded: A retailer customer review, because it was outside the critical-review sample
A review aggregator, because it summarised other people’s writing
An audiobook review, because it assessed a different edition and performance
A newspaper result available only as a partial extract, because its full argument could not be checked
Promotional and recommendation pages, because they did not provide a sustained critical argument
